I've been farming this land for nearly half a century. My husband and I know every corner of these 7 mu. The wheat-maize rotation is what I've always done — it's what my mother did, it's what the whole village does. There's no reason to change that.

For wheat, I'll plant in October like always, after the maize comes off. I'll hire the village tractor to plough deep — my back can't take heavy work anymore, and deep ploughing helps the roots. I buy seed from the township supply cooperative. They sell the same improved variety most neighbors use. I won't try something new I don't know.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer as base when I plant, then urea in spring when the wheat starts to green up. I know some younger farmers use less, but I've always done it this way and my yields are decent. I can't risk a poor harvest — it's just the two of us and we need the grain.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. The turnaround is fast so I only do rotary tillage. I always buy hybrid seed — haven't planted my own saved seed for maize in over twenty years, the hybrid grows much better. I top-dress urea when the stalks are knee-high.

Water I have from the well. I'll irrigate wheat four times — before winter freeze, before jointing, at heading, and once more if it's dry. Maize I irrigate when I see the leaves start to curl, and at tasseling. Three times is usually enough.

For pesticides, I spray herbicide early in both crops, and watch for aphids in wheat — last few years they've been bad. I spray what I need to, when I see the problem.
